newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies end lower but losses pared.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies end lower but losses pared.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures closed lower but losses were trimmed late, traders said.
The effects of higher grain futures and fund rolling somewhat offset a firmer cash outlook, sources noted.
Live hogs closed 0.475 cent per lb lower to 0.075 higher with April off 0.125 at 70.100 cents. Pork bellies ended 0.100 to 0.825 lower with May off 0.300 at 75.875 cents.

Sharp increases in grain futures which pushed CBOT March corn to a fresh 5-1/2 month high, losses in live cattle futures and active fund rolling kept a lid on April live hogs despite expectations for steady to higher cash hog prices Tuesday, traders said.
Packers need hogs as marketings have fallen short of expectations. They may also be more interested in obtaining hogs as cash pork prices were expected to bottom soon, they said.
"The low pork prices should increase retailer interest over beef," one trader said.
A settlement between union workers and the Rochelle Foods unit of Hormel Foods at Rochelle, Ill., was also viewed as supportive.
The threat of a strike loomed over the market until the union approved a new contract on Sunday.
But the "Goldman roll", rolling by the Goldman Sachs fund, weighed on April much of the day, traders added.
